siteMetadata.about:
I’m Nezar, a data scientist based in Paris and available remotely, with an engineering degree in Applied Mathematics and Computer Science from Polytech Sorbonne.
        I work across luxury & fashion analytics, healthcare and logistics, building classification, forecasting, recommendation and fraud-detection models, as well as NLP and LLM systems, from exploration to production. What interests me most is evaluation: knowing how well a model really performs before anyone relies on it, and having the statistics to back it up.
        In my free time, I enjoy long-distance running, traveling, and discovering new places, always on the lookout for fresh challenges to learn and grow.

projects.name: Derivation of Cochran's Formula for Sample Size Determination
projects.description: Derived Cochran’s formula by inverting the margin-of-error equation—leveraging the Central Limit Theorem to compute required sample sizes for means and proportions at a given confidence level.

projects.name: DeepOCT: Clinical Decision Support for Diabetic Macular Edema
projects.description: Built for the Faculty of Medicine and Pharmacy (CHU Ibn Sina), Rabat. OCT macular scans are denoised, then a self-hosted Qwen2-VL-72B extracts 8 biomarkers and a GPT-4o layer turns them into a diagnostic synthesis, treatment plan and anatomo-visual prognosis. Validated against two expert ophthalmologists on 100 annotated eyes, reaching 91.7% weighted F1 on biomarker detection and 87% overall agreement with expert reading. The two biomarkers the model under-identified were deliberately left editable by the clinician rather than auto-applied. A study prototype, not a deployed clinical tool.

projects.name: Ride-Hailing Trends in New York City: Uber, Lyft, and Via Operations Analysis
projects.description: Analyzed fare pricing, demand patterns, and borough-specific dynamics of Uber, Lyft, and Via in NYC using trip data from January to May 2021, uncovering insights into the competitive landscape and operational challenges.

projects.name: RAG Question-Answering on Natural Questions
projects.description: Open-domain QA over a self-built 19k-page / 469k-chunk Wikipedia corpus, cleaned by a 9-rule extraction pipeline that strips 51% of the raw text as boilerplate without ever cutting an answer span. Fine-tuned a 22M-parameter cross-encoder reranker on hard negatives mined by the retriever, lifting passage recall@5 from 69.1% to 81.1% and recall@10 from 79.8% to 88.6% on a held-out 1,626-question split, stratified by question type and grouped by page. Answers located inside tables are excluded, so the figures are not comparable to published NQ-Open numbers.

projects.name: Traffic Modeling and Forecasting Using Sensor Data in Paris
projects.description: Analyzed traffic patterns from 3,500 sensors in Paris to identify congestion trends and relationships between vehicle flow and road occupancy, with plans to build forecasting models and account for geographical dependencies.

frontmatter.title: Ride-Hailing Trends in New York City ( Uber, Lyft, and Via ) Operations Analysis
frontmatter.description: In this post, I cover the analysis of ride-hailing services in New York City, focusing on fare pricing and demand trends. Using trip data from NYC’s Taxi and Limousine Commission, I built models to predict fare prices with a decision tree regressor and forecast demand surges using the XGBoost algorithm. The fare prediction model achieved an R-squared value of 0.81, while the demand forecasting model produced accurate results with an RMSE of 2100. The study also classified NYC boroughs based on ride-hailing characteristics, providing actionable insights for better resource management.
